content: Consensus on agent orchestration: hybrid wins. Deterministic (code) orchestration at the workflow level, LLM execution at the task level, and narrow LLM routing only at semantic decision points. Rationale: control-flow decisions sampled from a distribution have per-step accuracy < 1, so error compounds over long horizons; failure modes are re-doing done work, skipping steps, terminating early. Reference architectures: Bernstein (Goal -> LLM planner ONCE -> task graph -> deterministic scheduler -> agents -> verifier -> merge; zero LLM tokens spent on coordination), and a five-phase deterministic phase machine where every transition is gated by an explicit verdict and no progress happens without acceptance. For long-horizon runs the common pattern is stateless sessions: deterministic orchestrator decides what runs and with what state, each session is a fresh LLM call, state lives in files (tasks/journal/progress), and a circuit breaker handles stuck detection plus a max-session cap. Design rule: deterministic router when stage structure is stable and known in advance; LLM only for goal decomposition and genuinely semantic decisions.
